scope.description: The same two trials as the predecessor over real four-voter clusters with one voter demoted to nonvoter: the leader is partitioned together with the nonvoter in one trial and alone in the control, the verification outcome, vote tally and quorum are recorded, and in the interrupted trial the detached voters' own leader and committed entry are compared with the interrupted leader's applied index. The only change is which prerequisite admits the peer-side comparison.
assumptions: Identical to the predecessor: captured in-memory timeouts, demotion through the exported DemoteVoter contract, reachability carried by the applied partition and by the detached voters' own election rather than by contact timestamps, and verification driven on the same channel the exported API uses.
The control trial intentionally ends without a peer-side event because in that case the voters are still led by the interrupted leader, so there is no detached quorum to observe.
excluded: No on-disk store, no network transport, no multi-process execution and no synthetic request injection.

basis.prefix: Unchanged from the predecessor harness: each trial builds a real four-voter cluster with the captured in-memory timeouts, demotes one follower to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits until the configuration shows it without a vote, verifies the healthy leader, applies one command, applies the partition, verifies again while recording the outcome, tally and quorum, and in the interrupted trial watches the two detached voters until one reports Leader, has it commit one entry, and records that index against the interrupted leader's applied index. No production file is modified and only the TestAssurance-prefixed test is selected.

comparisons.description: A leader that can exchange RPCs only with a nonvoter is confirmed as leader, with the tally reaching the voter quorum.
Control: the same leader with no peer at all is not confirmed.

Only for the interrupted trial, whose admitted prefix is the interrupted-case baseline: the voters the leader cannot reach elect a leader and commit an entry above the interrupted leader's applied index while the leader held a successful verification.

before.description: Two trials over real four-voter clusters with the in-memory transport: one voter is demoted to nonvoter with DemoteVoter, the leader is verified while healthy, and then in the interrupted trial the leader is partitioned together with the nonvoter while in the control trial the leader is partitioned alone. Each trial records the verification outcome, the vote tally and the quorum it was measured against, the suffrages on the leader's side of the partition, and - for the interrupted trial - whether the voters the leader cannot reach elected their own leader and committed an entry that the interrupted leader never applied.
assumptions: The in-memory transport is used with the captured in-memory timeouts, so the leader lease and election timers are the same ones the target's own tests use; this keeps the verification inside the window before the interrupted leader's own lease check steps it down.
The demotion goes through the exported DemoteVoter contract, so the configuration that produces three voters plus one nonvoter is produced by the target rather than written into a store by hand.

Reachability is not claimed from the contact timestamps: the leader-side suffrages are a property of the partition the harness applied, reported as such, and the observation that the other voters could not reach the leader is carried by their own election and commit.
Votes and quorum are read through the same in-package accessors the target's own tests use; the verification itself is driven through the same channel the exported VerifyLeader API uses.
excluded: No on-disk store, no network transport and no multi-process execution.
No injection of a synthetic request: every event comes from the target's own leader loop, replication goroutines and exported APIs.

prefix.before: Each trial builds a real four-voter cluster with MakeCluster and the captured in-memory timeouts, takes the elected leader, and demotes one follower to nonvoter with DemoteVoter, waiting until the leader's configuration shows that server without a vote. It then verifies the healthy leader through the same channel the exported VerifyLeader API uses, recording the outcome, the vote tally the future ended with and the quorum size from quorumSize(), plus how many peers had contacted the leader within the lease and which suffrages the harness is about to leave on the leader's side. It applies one command so the interrupted leader has a known FSM point, applies the partition, and verifies again, recording the same operands and the leader's state. In the interrupted trial it then watches the two voters that the partition detached from the leader until one of them reports Leader, has it commit one entry, and records that entry's index against the interrupted leader's applied index; the control trial stops after the second verification. Only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected and no production file is modified.
prefix.after: Unchanged from the predecessor harness: each trial builds a real four-voter cluster with the captured in-memory timeouts, demotes one follower to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits until the configuration shows it without a vote, verifies the healthy leader, applies one command, applies the partition, verifies again while recording the outcome, tally and quorum, and in the interrupted trial watches the two detached voters until one reports Leader, has it commit one entry, and records that index against the interrupted leader's applied index. No production file is modified and only the TestAssurance-prefixed test is selected.

before.description: A leader that can exchange RPCs only with a nonvoter is confirmed as leader, with the vote tally reaching the voter quorum.
Control: the same leader with no peer at all is not confirmed, so the confirmation in the other case depends on the nonvoter acknowledgement.

While the interrupted leader holds a successful verification, the voters it cannot reach elect a leader and commit an entry whose index is above the interrupted leader's applied index, so the confirmation is not a valid basis for a consistent read.

after.description: A leader that can exchange RPCs only with a nonvoter is confirmed as leader, with the tally reaching the voter quorum.
Control: the same leader with no peer at all is not confirmed.

Only for the interrupted trial, whose admitted prefix is the interrupted-case baseline: the voters the leader cannot reach elect a leader and commit an entry above the interrupted leader's applied index while the leader held a successful verification.

revision_reason: Admission structure only; the harness bytes are unchanged. The predecessor's third comparison was reported incomplete because its prerequisite alias admitted both trials' baseline events while the control trial deliberately emits no peer-side result, so the machinery recorded a missing admission for the control. This revision adds a second prerequisite alias for the interrupted case only (baseline events with nonvoter_reachable_only true) and admits that comparison through it, leaving the two verification comparisons on the original alias. A fresh execution is used because the declared comparison changed.
